learning.why: teacher's battery example made me think about shape staying same even when you turn it; now i get that sphere is 3D like football, circle is flat

end.summary:
Matched laddoo, football and dice with sphere/cube using roundness, thickness and equal faces.
Named cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere in practice; naming was shown on a why/new-situation question.
Recognised some 3D shapes when position or size changed; more checking is needed next time.
A cylinder lying down was repeatedly treated as a different shape; this was not corrected after the last time it appeared.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised matching everyday objects to cubes, cuboids and spheres, and used features such as equal square faces, length and roundness. They named the five shapes on a why/new-situation question. A mix-up remained about a cylinder lying down: it still needs practice as the same cylinder when only its position changes. At home, turn a bottle or battery upright and sideways and ask, “What shape is it, and what stayed the same?”
